title.narrative: Empowering Rural Young Women in Mukono

description.narrative:
Amplifying Marginalized Voices: Empowering Rural Young Women to Lead Change in Mukono
Marginalized young women in Mukono—especially young women with disabilities, young mothers, rural youth, and out-of-school girls—are excluded from decision-making despite high school dropout rates, limited services, and no youth council representation. This project will mobilize 200 young women to document their lived experiences and advocate for change. A 50-member youth-led coalition will lead community campaigns and policy dialogues,presenting evidence and recommendations on inclusive health services, education re-entry, governance representation, and increased youth funding, shifting power to those most affected.
Goal: Empower marginalized young women in Mukono District to advocate for their rights and influence local policy.
Objectives: Document barriers affecting 200 young women; build advocacy and policy skills of 50 leaders; form a youth-led district advocacy coalition; hold 4 policy dialogues with district stakeholders; develop and promote youth-led policy recommendations.
Activities: Participatory research, leadership training, coalition building, 6 community campaigns,4 advocacy dialogues, policy briefs, and radio talk shows amplifying youth voices.

participating-org.narrative:
Resilient Women Community Based Organization operates in Mukono District to empower women, youth, elderlies, PWDs, and vulnerable households. Its mission is to enhance socio-economic well-being through skills training, entrepreneurship, inclusive livelihoods, charity, and community education while promoting environmental protection, renewable energy, and green, intelligent building solutions.Guided by values of empowerment, inclusiveness, integrity, sustainability, and collaboration, the organization works to build resilient, self-reliant, and sustainable communities.
Resilient Women Community Based Organization
Resilient Women CBO is 95% youth-led(ages 18-35) with young people holding primary decision-making power.
General Assembly (45 Members): Highest body; 43 youth, 2 advisors. Approves strategy and policies quarterly.
Board of Directors (5 Members, 80% Women): Ages 24-38; 40% persons with disabilities. Provides governance oversight.
Executive Committee (7 Members, 95% Women): Ages 22-37. Manages operations and strategic decisions.
Project Team (95% Youth, 95% Women): Project Coordinator (28, woman with disability), Advocacy Officer (26), Research Officer (24), 4 Community Mobilizers (22-39), Finance Officer (30).
Volunteers (15 Members): 14 youth, 1 advisor support activities.
Young people control 100% of strategic, program, and budget decisions through democratic processes. Women hold 95% of staff positions. Marginalized young women occupy leadership roles, ensuring authentic representation.
